📄 Foreign Ministry spokesperson pays tribute to Lamerd martyrs

📌 Shiraz, IRNA — Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei has paid tribute to martyrs in Lamerd, Fars Province, during a one-day visit to the southern Iranian city, where he arrived on Saturday at the head of a delegation of domestic and foreign media representatives.

Baqaei visited the central cemetery and honored the memory of the martyrs, including those killed during the recent war imposed by the United States and the Israeli regime, following an official reception by local officials.
​
Baqaei described Lamerd as a symbol of resistance, victimhood, and the strength of the Iranian people against their adversaries.
​
He condemned the Lamerd war crimes after watching a documentary, honoring the martyrs and wishing the injured recovery. He also called the attack a crime against Iran and humanity, stressing that documenting it is essential to seek justice, establish accountability, and defend Iranians’ rights.
​
The spokesperson said he had traveled to the city to express appreciation to its residents and meet families of martyrs and veterans.
​
A missile attack on Lamerd on February 28, 2026, killed 21 civilians, including teenagers and children, while 100 others were injured.
​
During his visit, Baqaei and his delegation are scheduled to inspect residential areas and sports halls targeted in the attack.
​
The program includes a press conference with domestic and international media at the site where Lamerd residents were killed, as well as an evening address at a public gathering.
​
The visit aims to commemorate the victims while highlighting Lamerd’s resilience and the importance of honoring those who lost their lives in the US-Israeli terror attacks.

🔻 US has no authority to define terrorism: Tehran

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei says the United States, as the world’s main trainer and promoter of terrorism, has no authority to set standards for defining terrorism.

In a post on X on Saturday, Baqaei censured remarks by US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on the anniversary of the September 11 attacks, saying his narrative contained “fundamental contradictions.”
​
“You cannot wage aggression, carry out cowardly assassinations, and inflict civilian casualties while simultaneously claiming exclusive authority to define terrorism and determine whose violence is legitimate,” he wrote.
​
He said the perpetrators of the September 11 attacks were not Iranian, but “the very same people” whom the United States had organized and trained in previous decades.
​
Baqaei also denounced the US wars in Afghanistan and Iraq following the September 11 attacks, saying that what Washington carried out under the banner of the “war on terror” killed large numbers of innocent civilians and caused widespread destruction.
​
He further said Washington has used the anniversary of September 11 to justify what he called an “unlawful war” against Iran, saying the war involved the assassination of officials and attacks on civilians, including women and children.
​
In remarks commemorating the 25th anniversary of September 11, Hegseth claimed that the war of aggression against Iran was part of the United States’ so-called war on terror and touted the damage inflicted on Iran since the beginning of the war on February 28.
